extracted.intended_audience: potential readers, volunteer contributors, translators, donors, partners, and journalists interested in Global Voices
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational about page describing Global Voices’ mission, roles (reporting, translation, advocacy, training), governance, funding, contributor expectations, and licensing/republishing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Our multilingual newsroom team reports on people whose voices and experiences are rarely seen in mainstream media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global Voices leverages the power of the internet to tell stories that build understanding across borders; editorial mission emphasizes coverage of underrepresented voices and perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation accessibility (Lingua)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Lingua volunteers make our stories available in dozens of languages to ensure that language is not a barrier to understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation is volunteer-driven and multilingual coverage is a core operational practice; dozens of language editions are cited as part of reducing language barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advox advocacy focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Advox team advocates for free speech online, paying special attention to legal, technical and physical threats to people using the internet to speak out in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advox’s remit is advocacy and monitoring of threats to digital free expression; work is oriented toward practical/legal/technical defenses for online speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rising Voices empowerment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rising Voices provides training and mentorship to local underrepresented communities who want to tell their own stories using participatory media tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity-building and participatory media training/mentorship are explicit programmatic goals aimed at empowering local storytellers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributor compensation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in the case of specially commissioned projects, Global Voices does not compensate writers or translators financially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteer contribution is the default; exceptions exist for specially commissioned projects. The site also runs paid services (e.g., Translation Services project) for partner organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special projects operational limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Global Voices typically runs one or two active special projects at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given include the Civic Media Observatory and the Translation Services project (which can offer paid translation work to like-minded organizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Community contribution standard
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to writing and translating stories, our community of volunteer contributors provides a breadth of local knowledge and connects Global Voices with like-minded initiatives around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community engagement and local knowledge from volunteers are presented as essential to the organisation’s reporting, outreach, and project work; pages invite readers to 'Meet our contributors' and 'Join us'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Media and NGO partnerships are also a key component of Global Voices’ work as a community, a media organization, and a network of free expression advocates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation explicitly values collaborations with media and NGOs as part of fulfilling its mission; a 'Partner with Global Voices' pathway is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and governance diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Global Voices is led by a diverse, gender-balanced management, editorial and administrative team whose members come from many different countries and speak dozens of languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance includes a board of directors drawn from founders, community representatives, and influential innovators; board members serve without remuneration, indicating governance and conflict-of-interest norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status and funding transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Global Voices is incorporated in the Netherlands as Stichting Global Voices, a nonprofit foundation. We rely on independent grants, editorial commissions, and corporate and individual donations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists legal identifiers (address, RSIN number), points to annual reports and a Fundraising Ethics Policy, and directs readers to FAQs for more financial/organizational detail—indicating commitments to transparency about funding and legal structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and editorial policy presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-Pages include: Global Voices Manifesto; Editorial Code; Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ); Corrections and Edit Requests; Global Voices Policy on AI; Republishing Guidelines; Logos & Badges; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the about page does not reproduce these policies, it signposts the existence of an Editorial Code, corrections procedure, AI policy, and republishing guidelines—implying formal editorial standards, correction mechanisms, and content-use rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and attribution requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This site is licensed as Creative Commons Attribution 3.0. Please read our attribution policy to learn about freely redistributing our work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global Voices uses CC BY 3.0 (Some Rights Reserved) and provides an attribution policy for how to legally and properly reuse/redistribute content; republishing guidelines and logos/badges pages are linked for practical reuse instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer-based operational model
rubrics_metrics.description: Global Voices is an international, multilingual community of writers, translators, and human rights activists founded in 2004; the community consists largely of volunteer contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation relies primarily on volunteer labor for reporting and translation, runs limited paid services/projects, and solicits donor support to sustain ad-free multilingual journalism—information relevant to expectations for contributors and partners.
